description.narrative:
Svenska ambassaden har fått en förfrågan från The Carter Center och Liberia Election Observation Network (LEON) att finansiera projektet "Strengthening citizen voices to advance electoral reform and democratic governance" med 31 300 000 kronor under perioden 2021-2024.
Det övergripande målet för denna insats är att LEON år 2024 ska ha ökad kapacitet att på egen hand bidra till att stärka demokratiska val och informerade medborgare genom icke-partisk och evidensbaserad valobervation och granskning av demokratiska processer.
Denna projekperiod kommer att fokusera på följande områden:
1) Påverkansarbete inom konstitutionella reformer samt valreformer
2) Följa och rapportera arbetet inom den lagstiftande församlingen i syfte att öka transparens
3) Ansvarsskyldighet och medborgarengagemang
4) Genomföra diskussionsgrupper för att säkerställa medborgarnas bidrag till policy och reformer
5) Genomföra nationella enkätundersökningar som genererar policypåverkan
6) Bidra till diskussioner på länsnivå för att åtgärda bristen på tillgång till information utanför Monrovia
7) Genomföra valobservation i fyllnadsval och i det nationella valet 2023

The Carter Center and Liberia Election Observation Network (LEON) have applied to the Swedish Embassy for funding of 31 300 000 SEK to carry out the project "Strengthening citizen voices to advance electoral reform and democratic governance" during the period 2021-2024.
The overall goal of this intervention is that by 2024, LEON will have increased capacity to operate independently and will have contributed to the strengthening of democratic elections, governance, and an informed citizenry through credible non-partisan and evidence-based citizen observation around elections and democratic processes.
This project phase will focus on the following main areas of activity:
1. advocacy on electoral and constitutional reforms
2. monitoring the legislative branch to improve transparency
3. accountability, and citizen engagement
4. conducting discussion groups to ensure citizen input on legislative and government programs
5. conducting national surveys that generate results that can guide policy
6. facilitation of county-level discussions on key topics to address information gaps outside of Monrovia
7. observation of legislative by-elections and the 2023 national elections

The overall goal of this intervention is that by 2024, LEON will have increased capacity to operate independently and will have contributed to the strengthening of democratic elections, governance, and an informed citizenry through credible non-partisan and evidence-based citizen observation around elections and democratic processes. The intervention has two objectives: Objective 1: LEON has increased organizational capacity to manage projects and enhance their long-term sustainability. Objective 2: LEON is a credible and non-partisan organization that contributes to strengthening inclusive and participatory democratic processes and institutions in Liberia through programming in advocacy, election observation, surveys, and legislative monitoring.

description.narrative: The Carter Center Democracy Program has developed the capacity of the Liberia Elections Observation Network (LEON) to observe, advocate, and report on electoral, democratic, and governance processes in Liberia since before the 2017 general elections. The current project, Strengthening Citizen Voices to Advance Electoral Reform and Democratic Governance, initially spanned from July 2021 to June 2024. Sida then made the decision to extend the agreement with the Carter Center for a phaseout period until June 2025. Throughout the four year project period, LEONs main activity areas included advocacy around electoral reform observation of elections, including legislative byelections and the 2023 general elections conducting national public perception surveys to generate findings for guiding policy making monitoring the legislature to improve transparency, accountability, and citizen engagement social media monitoring and organizational strengthening and internal administrative, operational, and financial capacity building. In relation to objective 1, the project activities steadily strengthened LEON as an organization and enhanced its voice in areas of democracy and governance in Liberia. LEON achieved important successes in support of its strengthened capacity and sustainability. This included registration as a legal entity with the Government of Liberia in November 2022, a midline capacity assessment in March 2023 adoption of LEONs Constitution and updated organizational polices and operational procedures in May 2023 and an endline capacity assessment in March 2024. The Carter Center continued advising on implementation of LEONs sustainability plan that aimed to transition LEON into a self-sufficient organization capable of receiving direct donor funding. With support from The Carter Center, LEON improved efficiency, including adjusting staff roles and responsibilities, updating policies and procedures, and ensuring accurate and timely monthly and annual financial reporting. In mid2024, upon advise by Sida and support by the Carter Center, LEON restructured its organization to refocus its scope of activities and reduce its scale of operations to encourage long-term sustainability. In relation to objective 2, LEON progressed throughout the reporting period by observing pre-election processes, including observation of the social, economic, and political environment around Liberias 73 districts. LEON also observed the procurement of biometric voter registration (BVR) kits, the new BVR process itself, and civic and voter education around the BVR process. LEON conducted five nationwide surveys on invalid balloting to inform data-driven advocacy citizens perception of the Liberia National Police (LNP) issues around women's political participation perceptions before and after the 2023 general elections and views on constitutional and electoral reform, war and economic crimes courts, and constituency boundary delimitation. LEON continued to engage in electoral law reform and advocacy around women's political participation and candidacy. LEON also developed capacities in the areas of communication with a newly designed website, the launch of an ElecTalk panel discussion series, and more frequent sharing of information on social media. In total, LEON released 15 public reports and 11 press statements on Liberias democracy. Throughout the project period, LEON interacted with civil society, political and governmental actors, and domestic and international observer groups (e.g. NEC, ECC, EU, EISA, AU, and ECOWAS). LEON increased its respectability and has become a recognized source for reliable information. Different electoral stakeholders now engage regularly with LEON.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
